newsitem.title: USA: U.S. savings institutions lost $55 million in Q3.
newsitem.headline: U.S. savings institutions lost $55 million in Q3.

text.p: The 1,961 U.S. savings institutions insured by Federal Deposit Insurance Corp had a net loss of $55 million in the third quarter compared with profits of $2.6 billion in the previous quarter, FDIC reported Friday.

The bulk of the decline was due to special one-time assessments of $3.5 billion paid into the Savings Association Insurance Fund, FDIC said. Without the special assessments, the savings industry would have earned $2.2 billion, FDIC said.

Almost two out of every three savings institutions reported a net loss for the quarter, FDIC said. But among thrifts that did not have SAIF deposits, and therefore did not pay special assessments, only five percent were unprofitable for the quarter, FDIC said.
With the SAIF fund now fully capitalized, FDIC estimated thrifts with SAIF deposits will save about $875 million a year on deposit insurance premiums.
